advisory.title: `hugepage_rs::Box::new` may cause undefined behavior when initializing memory
advisory.description:
`hugepage_rs::Box::new` incorrectly initialized freshly allocated memory. Earlier implementations could either drop an uninitialized `T` or create a mutable reference before the memory contained a valid `T`, causing undefined behavior even when called from safe Rust code.

The issue was fixed in version `0.1.2` by using `ptr::write(nn.as_ptr(), data)` to initialize memory directly through a raw pointer.

advisory.title: `hugepage_rs::alloc` may cause undefined behavior with zero-sized layouts from safe code
advisory.description:
`hugepage_rs::alloc` was a publicly accessible safe function that forwarded a `Layout` to the hugepage allocator's `GlobalAlloc::alloc` implementation without enforcing its safety requirements.
`GlobalAlloc::alloc` requires the layout size to be non-zero. However, the safe wrapper allowed callers to pass a zero-sized `Layout`, violating this precondition without using `unsafe`.
Affected versions therefore exposed an unsafe allocation precondition through safe Rust code, violating Rust's soundness guarantees.

The upstream repository fixed this in version `0.1.2` by marking `alloc` as unsafe and documenting its non-zero-layout requirement.

advisory.title: `hugepage_rs::dealloc` may allow invalid memory deallocation from safe code
advisory.description:
`hugepage_rs::dealloc` was a publicly accessible safe function. It accepted an arbitrary raw pointer and `Layout`, then forwarded them to the hugepage allocator's `GlobalAlloc::dealloc` implementation.

`GlobalAlloc::dealloc` requires callers to ensure that the pointer denotes a block of memory currently allocated by the allocator and that the layout is the same layout used for the allocation. The safe wrapper neither verified these requirements nor marked them as
unsafe preconditions for callers.

Affected versions therefore allowed safe Rust code to call `dealloc` with an invalid pointer, a pointer not allocated by the hugepage allocator, or an incorrect layout, which could cause undefined behavior.

The upstream repository fixed this in version `0.1.1` by marking `dealloc` as unsafe and documenting the caller's safety requirements.
